name: How do I know the new bathtub surround will not leak?

mainEntity.name: How do I know the new bathtub surround will not leak?

acceptedAnswer.text:
A tub surround is not automatically waterproof simply because it is made from a water-resistant material. The wall system, seams, penetrations, transitions, substrate, and installation method must work together to direct water away from framing and finished walls.

Context: Tile surrounds and prefabricated panels use different installation approaches. The important question is how the complete wet-area assembly is prepared and sealed, not only whether the surface looks attractive.

Key factors:
- Substrate and waterproofing method
- Sealing at corners, fixtures, and tub flange
- Compatibility between tub and wall system
- Access around plumbing penetrations

Practical guidance: Ask for the proposed wall assembly and how penetrations, niches, shelves, and the tub-to-wall transition will be treated. Photograph concealed work before it is covered when possible.

Elite Remodeling & Design can coordinate tub, wall finish, plumbing, and design decisions as one bathroom construction scope.
acceptedAnswer.description: Ask how the substrate, waterproofing, seams, corners, fixture penetrations, tub flange, and wall transition will be handled. A water-resistant panel alone does not guarantee a watertight assembly. Confirm the installation system and document concealed work before finishes cover it.
